A's father's wife = A's mother (assuming same family).

A is the brother of B.

Answer: Brother

questions.question: A person standing on a railway platform notices that the sound of an approaching train's whistle changes in pitch (frequency) as the train passes by. This phenomenon is best explained by:
questions.questionHtml: A person standing on a railway platform notices that the sound of an approaching train's whistle changes in pitch (frequency) as the train passes by. This phenomenon is best explained by:
questions.solution:
When a source of sound moves relative to an observer, the observed frequency changes.

When the train approaches: frequency (pitch) appears higher.

When the train moves away: frequency appears lower.

This change in observed frequency due to relative motion between source and observer is called the Doppler Effect.

Initial ratio A : B : C = 7 : 8 : 5

Drained B = 8 × 2 = 16

B = 8x − 16

x − 17 = 25

Answer: 840 litres

options.text: It is alleged that the authorities halted the construction.
options.html: It is alleged that the authorities halted the construction.

options.text: The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.
options.html: The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.

options.text: The violation allegedly halted the construction.

questions.solution:
Original (Passive): The construction is alleged to have been halted...

The structure 'is alleged to have been halted' (passive infinitive perfect) becomes 'is alleged to have halted' (active infinitive perfect).

Subject change: 'The construction' (object of halting) becomes the object, 'The authorities' becomes the subject.

Active: The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.

Option 1: 'It is alleged that...' — impersonal construction, not a direct active voice conversion.

Option 2: Changes meaning (drops 'alleged').

Option 4: Subject changed to 'violation' — incorrect.

Answer: The authorities are alleged to have halted the construction.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: I am confident to pass the examination.
questions.solution:
'Confident' is followed by the preposition 'of' when used with a gerund (verb+ing).

Correct: 'I am confident of passing the examination.'

'Confident to pass' — incorrect; 'confident' does not take an infinitive.

'Confident in passing' — less standard but used for 'confident in one's ability'.

'Confident for' — incorrect preposition.

Answer: of passing the examination

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: You must adapt with the situation.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: You must adapt with the situation.
questions.solution:
The correct option is adapt to the situation.

Explanation: The verb adapt uses the preposition "to" when it means modifying your behavior to suit new conditions or environments (e.g., "adapt to the climate," "adapt to the changes"). The phrase "adapt with" is grammatically incorrect in this context.

Since the original sentence is "You must adapt with the situation," replacing the highlighted part ("adapt with the situation") completely yields "adapt to the situation" to make the sentence grammatically accurate: "You must adapt to the situation."

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. She said, "I had completed the report."
questions.questionHtml: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. She said, "I had completed the report."

options.text: She said that she completed the report.
options.html: She said that she completed the report.

options.text: She said that she has completed the report.
options.html: She said that she has completed the report.

options.text: She said that she had completed the report.
options.html: She said that she had completed the report.

options.text: She said she had been completing the report.
options.html: She said she had been completing the report.

questions.solution:
Direct speech: 'I had completed the report.' — Past Perfect tense.

Rule: When reporting speech with past reporting verb ('said'), Past Perfect remains as Past Perfect.

Past Perfect (had completed) → stays as Past Perfect (had completed) in indirect speech.

Indirect: She said that she had completed the report.

'She completed' — Simple Past, not correct here.

'She has completed' — Present Perfect, incorrect tense shift.

'Had been completing' — Past Perfect Continuous, changes meaning.

Answer: She said that she had completed the report.
